thread:
alex: quick question — we're seeing more requests to support typed protobufs end-to-end, but browser/mobile SDKs still need HTTP/JSON. do we keep a gateway that does proto<->json transcoding or force client SDKs to include lightweight proto support?

sam: my vote is gateway transcoding for now. lowers friction for product teams. :+1:

lina: gateway helps adoption but adds complexity to quota attribution & telemetry. we lose the original proto method name unless we attach extra headers. that's been a pain for console routing metrics.

maria: can we inject something like `x-internal-method` at the gateway so console can show method-level p50s? that would be a minimal change.

alex: yes that was my thought. gateway can add `x-routed-method: ModelService.Generate` after validating proto -> json mapping. need to be careful about spoofing though.

jonah: security check — if gateway injects headers we must only allow them from the gateway identity and strip inbound if present. otherwise quota evasion risk. ops should enforce in ingress filters.

devops-bot: note: ingress filter rule `strip-and-append` deployed to staging at 2024-09-30T18:10Z

sam: besides telemetry, there's also rollout UX in console. product wants a per-route toggle: "Allow JSON fallback" vs "Proto-only" with canary percentage. any thoughts on how that maps to runtime routing?

lina: runtime can route by header + route config. plan: add route config `proto_compatibility: { fallback_json: true, fallback_weight: 20 }` and brokers will probabilistically send to proto or json-transcoded service.

maria: console UX needs to show expected quota impact. if we transcode at the gateway we create additional CPU work — need to estimate token-equivalent cost increase. Redwood Optimize should be able to surface that.

alex: agree. also need an A/B signal in tracing so evicted requests (transcoded) are flagged. otherwise debug is messy.

jonah: curious about client ergonomics — if we ship a small proto-wasm for browsers, we can avoid transcoding costs but it'll be extra bundle size. mobile could include proto easily. tradeoff: cost vs adoption.

sam: product will lose momentum if engineers have to swap SDKs. gateway gives fastest velocity. we can plan a long-term path to proto-first and mark gateway as transitional.

lina: re: schema evolution — if gateway does mapping it needs to be tolerant to unknown fields or we'll break older clients. recommend using descriptor-set-based transcoder and feature flag strict_mode=false initially.

alex: can you sketch the minimal runtime changes?

lina: short version: (1) gateway receives JSON, (2) validates against proto descriptors, (3) converts to binary protobuf, adds `x-routed-method` and `x-proto-shape` header, (4) forwards to internal router. router uses header for routing/quota lookups. fallback path returns JSON and gateway converts back.

sam: sample config idea for console (RFC sketch):
```
routes:
  - name: generate-model
    path: /v1/generate
    proto_service: ModelService.Generate
    compatibility:
      json_fallback: true
      rollout_percent: 10
```

maria: nice. console can show a slider for rollout_percent + a perf estimate. we should add a telemetry call that runs a small probe (1% synthetic) to measure real CPU overhead of transcoding.

jonah: operators: when we do canary increase, we need circuit breakers if transcoder latency spikes. gateway should have `max_transcode_ms` config per route and abort to a `fail-open` or `reject-with-503` policy. product might prefer fail-open to keep UX intact, but that hides issues.

alex: let's default to fail-open with metric alerting, and offer enterprise customers strict mode that rejects on transcode exceed.

lina: one more: quota attribution. if gateway converts json->proto, should we attribute quota based on `x-routed-method` or the original path? Need to decide for billing accuracy.

maria: attribute to the canonical proto method for internal metrics + billing. but store raw request shape for audits. also update billing docs.

sam: ops question: does any team rely on current path-based quotas? changing attribution will affect customers. we need a migration window.

alex: good call — migration plan: start with dual-attribution (increment both path-based and proto-method counters) for 30 days, publish a console migration notice, then flip.

jonah: final infra ask: add sampling tag `transcoded=true/false` into traces and set a metric `gateway_transcode_latency_ms` with route label. that should make console dashboards easy.

lina: will add the telemetry labels. also adding a small cheat-sheet for SDK teams: pros/cons for proto-wasm vs gateway fallback.

maria: can someone file an RFC? I'll help with billing/migration text.

alex: I'll open RFC and include canary plan + console mockups. thanks all. :rocket:
